evidence.explanation: The opening drum break and horn stab of “Low Tide Signal” are looped under the first verse of “Glass Harbor”. The original recording itself is used.
“Signal Fire” re-sings the chorus melody and lyric of “Low Tide Signal” with new instrumentation. No audio from the 1974 recording is used, so the link is to the composition.
The hook of “Night Bus Hymn” re-performs the melody of the “Paper Moons Over Ohio” chorus with rewritten lyrics.
A slowed harp figure from “Copper Rain” runs through the whole of “Satellite Lullaby”.
A two-bar keyboard phrase in “Fever Almanac” closely resembles the intro of “Neon Psalm”.
evidence.caveat: The demo liner notes credit a sample, but the demo label catalog lists no clearance and the producer described the part as replayed. Treat as unconfirmed.

evidence.explanation: A fan post says the horn loop in “Loose Tape No. 4” comes from “Brass for the Weary”.
evidence.caveat: Only a fictional forum post names this sample. There are no liner notes or clearance records in the demo data.

evidence.explanation: The verse melody of “Ceiling Fan Gospel” is adapted from the main theme of “Sundial Waltz”, moved into 4/4.
Static Garden sample their own 2004 recording: a reversed vocal from “Ghost Frequencies” becomes the pad in “Quiet Machinery”.
The guitar intro of “Glass Harbor” is chopped into the beat of “Saltwater Receipts”. The sample passes through “Glass Harbor”, which itself samples “Low Tide Signal”.
A single plucked harp chord from “Copper Rain” is pitched down and repeated in the bridge of “Borrowed Light”.
The piano introduction of “Porchlight Standard” quotes the first eight bars of the “Sundial Waltz” theme.
The vocal run at the end of “Dial Tone Heart” is sampled and looped as the hook of “Undertone”. June Okafor-Lind is also credited as a writer.
